messages:
From: Diego Alvarez <diego@cloudscale-partners.com>

Cc: channel@cloudscale-partners.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Distributor tiering and waterfall for GCP private offer

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the time last week. We have a potential GCP private offer coming up with a mid-market customer (estimate $180k ARR first year) and CloudScale needs clarity on how Redwood wants to structure distributor/reseller economics for marketplace private offers. High level asks from our side:

- Commission waterfall: what % to distributor vs reseller vs sub-reseller at 3 tiers (0-250k / 250-1M / 1M+).
- Private offer uplift: any standard marketplace fee Redwood expects to retain versus pass-through?
- Billing & invoicing: can CloudScale invoice the customer and take a consolidated invoice, or does Redwood require marketplace billing?
- Minimum commit discounts: are uplifted discounts available for 12/24 month commits?

I attached a quick GCP PO template and a proposed waterfall that the channel team prefers. Can you confirm what ranges are possible (and which would need finance/lead approval)? Our partner ops lead is copied.

Short is fine — we need a statement of playbook so we can scope the customer procurement timeline.

Best,
Diego
Channel Partnerships, CloudScale Partners

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Distributor tiering and waterfall for GCP private offer

Diego — thanks for the concise outline and the attachments. Quick answers inline before I loop finance: 

- Commission waterfall: Redwood's starting framework for private offers is 12% to the primary distributor, 6% to downstream reseller (if registered) and an additional 2-4% optional sub-reseller kickback depending on enablement. That is for the 0-250k tier. For 250-1M we target 10% / 5% / 2-3%. For 1M+ we can move to 8% / 4% / 2% but those need a written commitment and review.

- Marketplace uplift: Redwood typically retains the marketplace fee (2-3% on GCP) but offsets this when a partner accepts consolidated invoicing; effectively we can reduce our service fee by 1% for partner-led billing. Any other marketplace charges are passed through.

- Billing: we support both (1) consolidated partner invoice under a reseller agreement, or (2) direct marketplace billing. For partner invoice option we need a reseller addendum and PO on file; monthly reconciliation and a 30-day payment term.

- Commit discounts: standard is 7% off list for a 12-month committed ARR band and 12% for 24-months, both available if commit >= $250k ARR. Deep discounts (15%+) require RevOps + leadership approval.

I'm looping Marcus (channel GTM) and Marissa (marketplace ops) to confirm these are publishable and to flag anything that needs a formal private-offer template or legal redline. If that works, Diego, can you share the customer's expected 12/24 month profile and preferred billing flow?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Channel Sales, Redwood Inference

Kimberly / Diego — quick follow from channel ops side. Couple of clarifications: 

1) The uplifts Kim mentioned (marketplace fee retention offset) are fine, but for partner consolidated invoicing we require a $25k onboarding fee to cover reconciliation tooling (one-time). We can waive this for strategic programs but need approval.

2) For the commission waterfall, we prefer setting explicit thresholds in the private offer doc rather than vague ranges — that'll prevent downstream disputes. I'm proposing we lock the following as default unless the partner requests otherwise and CC approves: 
   - Tier A (0-250k): Distributor 12% / Reseller 6% / Sub 2%
   - Tier B (250k-1M): Distributor 10% / Reseller 5% / Sub 2%
   - Tier C (1M+): Distributor 8% / Reseller 4% / Sub 1.5% (requires signed 12/24 month commit)

3) Billing model: if CloudScale invoices customer (partner-led), Redwood issues net-30 invoice to CloudScale monthly and provides per-customer usage reports. If GCP billing, Redwood pays GCP fees and bills partner for margin.

Rishi — tagging finance. Can you flag whether the 12/24 month commit discounts (7%/12%) are OK to publish as standard? If not, we'll require RevOps approval per-deal.

Marcus
Director, Channel GTM

Thanks Marcus — helpful. A few quick points from CloudScale ops: 

- The $25k onboarding fee is a blocker for this customer unless you can waive or amortize it across a 12-month commit. Their procurement expects no one-time onboarding line items. Could Redwood consider amortizing the fee at $2k/mo over 12 months if commit >= $250k ARR?

- The partner prefers distributor at 15% for Tier A (they run the deal and take most of the sales/enablement risk). Is there flexibility for a one-off elevated distributor rate if we reduce Redwood's list price in the private offer?

- For billing, customer prefers partner invoicing. We'll upload the PO once we finalize the waterfall and confirm invoicing cadence.

If we can get a yes on amortized onboarding and a one-off elevated Tier A distributor rate (subject to cap), we can sign terms this month.

Best,
Diego

Diego — appreciate the quick follow. Here's what Redwood can confirm today (so you can brief procurement):

- Onboarding fee: we can amortize the $25k onboarding fee across 12 months at $2,083/mo if the customer signs a 12-month commit >= $250k ARR. For 24 months we can amortize over 24 months. We'll note the amortization schedule in the reseller addendum.

- One-off elevated distributor rate: we can approve a one-time Tier A distributor rate up to 15% provided CloudScale accepts a 5% reduction in Redwood list price for that private offer (effectively a combined delta we track for finance).
